draft.title: Belief systems and identity
card: A belief system can shape how people see themselves. A person may say "I am a Buddhist" or "I am a Muslim" and feel that this says who they are.
Identity
a sense of who a person is and what groups they belong to. Shared beliefs, symbols and practices can be part of it.
Community
people who share a belief system often meet, celebrate and support one another. This gives them a sense of belonging.
Guidance
a belief system can offer guidance on how to act, such as how to treat others, what to eat or how to mark life events.
draft.remember: A belief system can give a person a sense of who they are, who they belong with and how to act.

a.q: Amira goes to her mosque each week and has friends there who support her. Which effect of her belief system does this show most directly?
opts: A sense of community and belonging
A rule for how to treat strangers
A way of explaining her own identity
A guide to what she should eat
a.why: Meeting with others who share her beliefs and being supported by them is community. Identity is about how she sees herself, not about the group that supports her, so it is the tempting wrong choice here.
a.clue: Focus on the friends who share her beliefs.

b.q: Tom's family follow a belief system that sets out how to greet elders and how to mark a birth. Which effect of the belief system is this?
opts: Guidance on how to act
A sense of community
A challenge to those in power
A change in his beliefs over time
b.why: Rules about greeting elders and marking a birth tell people how to act. The family may also share a community, but the detail given is about instructions for behaviour, not belonging.
b.clue: Look at what the beliefs tell people to do.

a.best: A sense of community and belonging
